### Subject: Opinion on point of taxation of capital gains on a Joint Development Agreement under Section 45(5A)

---

## 2. Statement of Facts

Mr. Suresh Iyer, an individual holding an ancestral plot as a capital asset, entered into a registered Joint Development Agreement with Skyline Builders LLP, under which he will receive 40% of the constructed area plus INR 50 lakh in cash, in exchange for development rights. The completion certificate for the project is expected approximately three years hence.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

When does capital gains tax arise on entry into the JDA, and how should the cash and constructed-area components be treated?

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 45(5A)
- Section 194-IC


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- CIT v. Balbir Singh Maini, (2017) 398 ITR 531 (SC)

## 6. Analysis

Section 45(5A) defers the capital gains tax trigger, for individuals and HUFs who do not transfer their share of the constructed area before completion, to the year in which the completion certificate for the project (or relevant part) is issued by the competent authority, superseding the earlier possession-based trigger discussed in Balbir Singh Maini. The stamp duty value of the constructed area received, together with any cash consideration, forms the basis for computing the deferred gain, while the developer is separately required to withhold tax under Section 194-IC on the cash component at the time of payment.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

Capital gains on the JDA are deferred to the year in which the completion certificate is issued; Skyline Builders LLP must withhold tax under Section 194-IC on the INR 50 lakh cash component at the time of payment.

**Confidence level:** High
